title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the surrounding pages). X is a smooth space or stack, eventually a moduli stack M_{g,ν}. Its boundary is a divisor D with normal crossings, with branches indexed by d. A simplex Δ_r = (d_0,…,d_r) indexes the intersection D_{Δr} = D_{d0}∩…∩D_{dr}. D*_{Δr} is the corresponding open stratum. Π_{Δr} is the fundamental groupoid of D*_{Δr}. Π̃_{Δr} is the fundamental groupoid of the punctured tubular neighbourhood of D*_{Δr}, a (C*)^{r+1}-type torus bundle over the stratum. Equivalently, Π̃_{Δr} is the 'π1 at infinity along that stratum', and there is a natural map Π̃_{Δr} → Π_{Δr}.

The previous page builds, for degeneracy-type maps α: Δ_r → Δ_{r'} with α(0)=0, 2-cartesian squares between Π̃ → Π. The horizontal maps are injective on π1 with finite index (finite covers). It concludes that all this is 'formal and trivial' and would hold for any stratified situation.

This page:
(i) It is the open strata D*_{Δr}, not the closed D_{Δr}, that serve to define Π and Π̃.
(ii) Fix d_0. The systems Π̃_{d0 d1…dr} → Π_{d0…dr} then form a tower of semi-simplicial groupoids. This structure is again essentially formal or trivial. Grothendieck nevertheless notes that this 'so-called triviality' should be examined more closely. It should be expressible via Galois theory of the coverings of D*_{d0}, resp. of the punctured neighbourhood P*_{d0}.
(iii) He announces a genuinely non-formal piece of structure. It uses the normal-crossings (transversal intersection) hypothesis in an essential way. The punctured-neighbourhood groupoids Π̃_{Δr} — and explicitly NOT the stratum groupoids Π_{Δr} — form a semi-simplicial groupoid as Δ_r varies.

The next page makes this concrete. For a face map α: Δ_r → Δ_{r'}, one needs a homomorphism Π̃_{Δr'} → Π̃_{Δr} (written with target Π_{Δr} there, probably a slip). It goes from the deeper stratum to the shallower one and is given by the specialization (cospecialization) homomorphism. Near a point of the deeper stratum, the punctured neighbourhood (a product of punctured discs) maps into the punctured neighbourhood of a shallower stratum.

The purpose is to assemble the 'structure at infinity' of M_{g,ν} as a diagram of tangential/boundary fundamental groupoids indexed by the nerve of the boundary stratification. The homotopy colimit of this diagram should model the link at infinity. This is the combinatorial-groupoid skeleton behind the Teichmüller tower and tangential base points of the Esquisse.
errors: No mathematical error on this page. The reverse functoriality (deeper → shallower for Π̃) is correct for normal crossings. It is indeed not available for the Π_{Δr} themselves; one only has an exit-path-type relation there, not a semi-simplicial groupoid in the same direction.
On the next page, the boxed arrow has target Π_{Δr} where Π̃_{Δr} is evidently meant (or the transcription is wrong).

ideas.what: Fundamental groupoids of open strata and of punctured tubular neighbourhoods of strata of a normal crossings boundary, related by 2-cartesian squares under degeneracies
ideas.modern_name: Local fundamental groups at infinity / log (Kato–Nakayama) fundamental groupoids of strata; tangential base points
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (tangential base points, 1989); Kato–Nakayama (1999); Ihara–Nakamura for M_{g,n} boundary
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses 'structure à l'infini' and tangential base points informally; SGA1 XIII (tame fundamental group along NCD, Grothendieck–Murre) is the algebraic background

ideas.what: The groupoids Π̃_{Δr} form a semi-simplicial groupoid over the nerve of the boundary strata via specialization maps, using normal crossings essentially; the Π_{Δr} do not
ideas.modern_name: Diagram of link groupoids over the stratification poset; exit-path / constructible-stack description of the homotopy type at infinity; boundary of the Kato–Nakayama / Borel–Serre-type real blow-up as a homotopy colimit
ideas.usually_credited_to: Exit paths: MacPherson, Treumann (2009), Lurie (HA); boundary π1 of M_{g,n}: Ihara–Nakamura, Nakamura (1990s); homotopy colimit descriptions of links of NCD: folklore (Durfee, A'Campo, etc.)
ideas.where_published: Not in a published Grothendieck text as far as I know; the Esquisse only alludes to it

ideas.what: Remark that the formal semi-simplicial tower for fixed d_0 should be analysed via Galois theory of coverings of D*_{d0} and of P*_{d0}
ideas.modern_name: Galois-theoretic description of tame coverings near a boundary component (Abhyankar lemma / log étale coverings)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck–Murre (1971); log étale fundamental group: Illusie, Fujiwara–Kato

missed.claim: Grothendieck isolates, as the key non-formal ingredient of the 'structure at infinity', a semi-simplicial structure on punctured-neighbourhood groupoids. It is contravariant in the face inclusions, comes from specialization, and needs the normal-crossings hypothesis. This anticipates the later organisation of boundary fundamental groupoids of M_{g,n} (Ihara–Nakamura, Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps) and exit-path/hocolim descriptions of links of NCD, explicitly as a semi-simplicial diagram of groupoids.
missed.quote: s'exprimant par le fait que les Π̃_{Δr} (NB et non les Π_{Δr} !) forment un groupoïde semi-simplicial, pour Δr variable
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a clean, discrete-groupoid formulation of the homotopy type at infinity of M_{g,n}. It could serve as a combinatorial input for Grothendieck–Teichmüller actions on the boundary. Mostly it is a known circle of ideas, so the novelty is modest.

missed.claim: He proposes to examine the 'so-called triviality' of the fixed-d_0 tower in Galois-theoretic terms (coverings of D*_{d0} vs P*_{d0}) and does not carry it out here.
missed.quote: il faudrait cependant examiner ... cette soi-disant trivialité ... en termes de la théorie de Galois des revêtements de D*_{d0} resp. de P*_{d0}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Minor; it is likely recoverable from log étale fundamental group theory.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a transitional, programmatic page. Its one real point is the insistence that the punctured-neighbourhood groupoids, not the stratum groupoids, carry a semi-simplicial structure via specialization. This is a nice, explicit organising principle for the structure at infinity of M_{g,ν} that is not in published Grothendieck texts. However, it corresponds to ideas later developed by others (tangential base points, boundary π1 of moduli, exit paths), so it is only mildly notable.
transcription_corrections: Line 2: 'semblent' is written above a struck word; the reading 'seuls/seules jouent un rôle particulier' is also possible.
Line 3: 'Pour d_0 fixé, les systèmes' — 'systèmes' is fairly secure; the lone '{+et+}.' is a stray insertion mark.
'mais des intervalles[?] constants[?] triviaux' is more plausibly 'mais de nature essentiellement triviale' (echoing the previous page's 'nature essentiellement formelle et triviale').
'cette mi-discrète[?] trivialité' is likely 'cette soi-disant trivialité'.
'y a-t-il[?] application[?] aux groupes[?] en termes de' is likely 'et elles s'explicitent [or s'expliquent] en termes de la théorie de Galois'.

'quitte à y obtenir[?] grâce aux[?] hypothèses de connexions[?] d'intersections normales' is likely '... non-formel, faisant intervenir les hypothèses de croisements normaux / d'intersections normales'.
Last line 'pour Δr variable. En d'autres' continues to 'termes' on the next page; correct.
